title: Numerical domain and boundary convergence
question: Could numerical-domain choices be creating or moving the higher states?
pass_condition: Every state energy is reported against each numerical knob, and each state is labelled converged or not-converged under an explicit tolerance. A physical state must not depend strongly on the outer boundary; any state that moves with the padding, the outer barrier width or the boundary condition is recorded as a numerical artifact of the Dirichlet box, not as physics. PASS is reached when every state carries that label.

controlled_change.summary: One numerical knob per deck, against the shared Demo 23 baseline. The sub-demo owns several knobs because the question is about the numerical domain as a whole, but no single deck turns more than one of them - except the state-count deck, where raising the number of states written requires raising the number solved.

decks.name: mesh_fine_0p025nm
decks.question: Is the 0.05 nm active mesh converged?

decks.name: mesh_coarse_0p100nm
decks.question: How far does a coarser mesh move the states? (sets the convergence slope)

decks.name: padding_4nm
decks.question: Do the states depend on where the Dirichlet walls are placed?

decks.name: padding_8nm
decks.question: Same question, further out - a physical state must stop moving

decks.name: outer_barrier_28p2nm
decks.question: Does a thicker outer barrier change the high states or the continuum onset?

decks.name: states_24
decks.question: Does simply asking for more states create new levels below the ones we use?

decks.name: boundary_neumann
decks.question: Is any state an artifact of the Dirichlet wall rather than of the barriers?
